minutes.headline: Conservation agent Herlin goes full-time Feb 9; trail grooming approved only on mapped trails
minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission worked through a long slate of tree-removal determinations, wetlands hearings and trail-grooming requests, approving most as presented and continuing several that lacked complete plans or abutter permission. The commission also confirmed the town's conservation agent will move to full-time starting in February, and touched on budgeting for a public information flyer, a snowmobile-grooming season, and utility/heating costs at the Hollis Road property.

budget_items.topic: Purchase order for Unitil utility bills, Hollis Road residence
budget_items.what_was_said: The business manager asked for a standing PO so monthly Unitil bills don't each need separate approval; the commission discussed raising the requested amount in case winter rates rise.

budget_items.topic: Heating system servicing, Hollis Road residence
budget_items.what_was_said: Annual furnace cleaning and filter service was reminded as scheduled for the end of the month, referencing a prior vote authorizing the expense; no site access needed since the tech uses the bulkhead.

A commissioner proposed budgeting to print and include the two-sided buffer-zone flyer in a town tax mailing so property owners are reminded of permit requirements; cost still needs a quote from the tax and printing departments.

budget_items.topic: Grant funding for Reo and Table Rock parking lots
budget_items.what_was_said: A former commissioner is preparing grant proposals to Mass Recreational Trails to fund parking-lot installation, citing Earth Day volunteer turnout as evidence of community support for the application.

transfers.description: Purchase order opened to cover recurring Unitil utility bills at the Hollis Road conservation property

decisions.decision: Continued hearings awaiting outside documentation (e.g., abutter permission) stay on the agenda for tracking, but will only be continued further at the applicant's or engineer's request.
Commission accepted the agent's reading that the proposed well-abandonment work at the Route 2A/13 site is exempt from wetlands performance standards and needs no permit or further commission action.
Commission agreed to add the buffer-zone information flyer/mailing as a budgeted line item for the coming fiscal year.

what_happened.line: The commission confirmed conservation agent Herlin will become full-time starting February 9.
Snow-dog grooming was approved for a year on the Lane property and Large Town Forest, but only on mapped trails, not private land.
A newer Table Rock trail map was adopted as the sanctioned groomable trails, excluding gray-shaded private land.
Four hearings, including a Mulpus Brook culvert replacement pending abutter right-of-entry permission, were continued to January 21, 2026 for missing documentation.
The commission agreed to add a buffer-zone information flyer as a budgeted line item for the coming fiscal year, cost still to be quoted.

why_it_matters: Trail users, including hikers, skiers and snowmobilers, gain a defined grooming season but only on town-mapped routes, not adjoining private land.
Property owners with pending wetlands or tree-removal applications near Spring Street, Summer Street, Northfield Road and Fire Road 15A will see those cases return January 21.
A conservation-agent staffing change and a proposed mailing flyer are small additions that could show up in next year's conservation budget line.
